claims.claim: Live Node fixture bundle generation and minimal VM restore
claims.notes: Proven by live Node fixtures; not surfaced as Goal 45 product support.

claims.claim: Node production, expanded, complex, and ecosystem cross-architecture restore envelopes
claims.notes: Goal 49 keeps the clean Node HTTP service subset productized through the shared clean-service contract using machinen snapshot <vm> <bundle> and machinen restore <bundle> with no runtime-specific flags.

claims.claim: Selected semantic Node Memory IR materialization through portable VM product snapshot/restore
claims.notes: Scoped caniuse-style matrix support for selected semantic Node Memory IR rows (string, nested object graph, shared references, cycle, Map/Set, class instance, Buffer, TypedArray) through machinen snapshot <vm> --portable --out <bundle> and machinen restore <bundle> --json. Evidence is retained for detect -> capture -> decode -> classify -> materialize -> verify -> retain and for arm64<->amd64 target-native materialization. This does not claim arbitrary Node process restore, raw V8 heap restore, same-PID continuation, arbitrary Linux process restore, or raw VM/vCPU/device replay.

claims.claim: Node/V8/libuv single-thread HTTP counter selected-state reconstruction harness
claims.notes: Harness proof only: snapshot captures the app-specific node-http-counter-selected-state-v1 descriptor and restore verifies target-native Node serves the continued count. This is not Level 5 product support because it does not reconstruct captured source process/runtime/native state.

claims.claim: Node unsafe neighbors: active ambiguous sockets, child/IPC trees outside contract, inspector sessions, native addon ABI drift, dirty persistent state, package provenance drift, lifecycle/network install ambiguity
claims.notes: Stable refusal codes remain authoritative and must keep migrationCompleted=false.

claims.claim: JVM, Python, Ruby, and Go service runtime envelopes
claims.notes: Goal 49 productizes the clean Python HTTP service subset through the shared clean-service contract using machinen snapshot <vm> <bundle> and machinen restore <bundle> with no runtime-specific flags; Ruby/JVM portions remain proof-only until separately graduated.

claims.claim: Go static HTTP clean-service cross-architecture restore
claims.notes: Goal 49 adds go-http-clean-root-v1 for statically linked Go HTTP services with cgo and dynamic linkage refused.
Quiescent goroutine/channel/timer proof remains a fixture-level support envelope.

claims.claim: Hard runtime-state boundaries for active TLS, opaque native extension state, arbitrary Go scheduler state, JNI/cgo/native gems/C extensions, and refusal UX catalog
claims.notes: These states remain refused by product support unless a future explicit portable contract and verifier graduates them.

claims.claim: Ping sequence/counter semantic continuation across arm64 and amd64
claims.notes: Retired as product support by Goal 011. Ping product support now goes through the portable machine Level 4 socket reconstruction path instead of a ping-specific Level 2 semantic continuation.

claims.claim: Ping/raw ICMP socket Level 4 reconstruction across arm64 and amd64
claims.notes: Narrow Level 4 product route through the portable machine snapshot path for datagram ping sockets and raw ICMP sockets with empty receive queues, no in-flight packets, no active recvmsg, unambiguous loopback route/namespace, credential/capability mapping, and target-native verifier evidence.

claims.claim: Eventfd counter Level 4 reconstruction across arm64 and amd64
claims.notes: Narrow Level 4 product route through the generic portable restore adapter path for bounded nonzero eventfd counters with semaphore mode off, waiters known empty, no aliases, close-on-exec only, and target-native verifier evidence.

claims.claim: Empty pipe pair Level 4 reconstruction across arm64 and amd64
claims.notes: Narrow Level 4 product route through the generic portable restore adapter path for empty pipe pairs with exactly one read end and one write end, open peer lifetime, no waiters, known not-readable readiness, close-on-exec only, and target-native verifier evidence.

claims.claim: Relative one-shot timerfd Level 4 reconstruction across arm64 and amd64
claims.notes: Narrow Level 4 product route through the generic portable restore adapter path for CLOCK_MONOTONIC relative one-shot timerfds with bounded remaining time, no unread expirations, no interval, close-on-exec only, and target-native verifier evidence.

claims.claim: Loopback TCP listener-only Level 4 reconstruction across arm64 and amd64
claims.notes: Narrow Level 4 product route through the generic portable restore adapter path for 127.0.0.1 TCP listeners with static port, explicit backlog, empty accept queue, SO_REUSEADDR, no active connections, and target-native verifier evidence.

claims.claim: PostgreSQL clean/quiesced logical restore arm64 -> amd64 and amd64 -> arm64
claims.notes: Goal 45 productized this through a separate capture-style workflow; it is not advertised as implemented Goal 47 snapshot/restore support until it uses machinen snapshot <vm> <bundle> without extra runtime flags.

claims.claim: PostgreSQL active transaction/session, dirty WAL, torn data directory, replication, external extension/native plugin, host-mounted data directory, and physical data-directory/WAL byte-copy
claims.notes: Product capture/restore keeps active transaction/session, dirty WAL, host-mounted data-dir, and physical copy refusals stable; broader PostgreSQL refusal profiles remain proof-matrix refusals.

claims.claim: Redis, SQLite, expanded PostgreSQL, MySQL/MariaDB, durable queue, and filesystem-backed stateful service matrices
claims.notes: Stateful-service matrix remains proof evidence except for the selected PostgreSQL logical subset productized in Goal 45.

claims.claim: Stateful service unsafe neighbors: active clients, hot WAL/journals, redo/AOF ambiguity, replication/plugin state, mmap/lock/unsynced host-mounted filesystem ambiguity
claims.notes: Fail-closed semantics and migrationCompleted=false remain required for product paths.
